title: More than one
summary: Make broken plurals such as صُحُون and مَلَاعِق, and give plurals of things a feminine adjective.
intro: Most Arabic plurals are not made with an ending: the inside of the word changes. كِتَاب (book) becomes كُتُب, قَلَم (pen) becomes أَقْلَام, and صَحْن (plate) becomes صُحُون. These are the broken plurals. There are common patterns, but the best way is to learn every noun together with its plural. One more rule: the plural of a thing is treated as feminine singular, so 'the plates are big' is الصُّحُون كَبِيرَة.
objectives: Name eight things on a dinner table and give their plurals
Recognise the plurals of words you already know, such as كُتُب and بُيُوت
Describe plurals of things with a feminine adjective
Count plates and glasses from three to ten

realLife.title: Dinner at Sami's house
realLife.story: Sami's mother Fatima invites Daniel and Layla to dinner. The whole family is there, so there are seven people at the table. Layla and Daniel help to lay the table: plates, glasses, spoons, forks and a lot of bread.

mistakes.why: The plural of a thing is treated as feminine singular, so the adjective takes ة: jadīda.

sentences.en: The plates are on the table.
We have ten loaves of bread.

mistakes.why: After the numbers three to ten the noun is plural.

sentences.en: Where are the spoons? They are in the kitchen.
sentences.literal: where (are) the spoons? she (is) in the kitchen

mistakes.why: For a plural of things use هِيَ ('she, it'). هُمْ ('they') is only for people.

sentences.en: I have many friends in Cairo.
sentences.literal: at me (are) friends many in Cairo

dialogue.title: Seven plates, seven glasses
dialogue.culture: Egyptian hosts say الْبَيْت بَيْتُكُمْ, 'the house is your house', and keep offering more food: refusing once is only polite, so expect to hear كُلُوا again. Young people call a friend's mother خَالَة (auntie), even when she is not a relative.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا! الْبَيْت بَيْتُكُمْ. الْعَشَاء جَاهِز بَعْدَ قَلِيل.
lines.en: Welcome! Make yourselves at home. Dinner will be ready in a moment.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا خَالَة فَاطِمَة! هَلْ نُسَاعِدُكِ فِي شَيْء؟
lines.en: Thank you, Auntie Fatima! Can we help you with anything?

lines.ar: نَعَم، شُكْرًا! الصُّحُون وَالْأَكْوَاب فِي الْمَطْبَخ، عَلَى الطَّاوِلَة الصَّغِيرَة.
lines.en: Yes, thank you! The plates and glasses are in the kitchen, on the small table.

lines.ar: نَحْنُ سَبْعَة أَشْخَاص الْيَوْم، إِذَنْ نُرِيدُ سَبْعَةَ صُحُون.
lines.en: We are seven people today, so we need seven plates.

lines.ar: هٰذِهِ سَبْعَة صُحُون كَبِيرَة، وَسَبْعَة أَكْوَاب. أَيْنَ الْمَلَاعِق؟
lines.en: Here are seven big plates and seven glasses. Where are the spoons?

lines.ar: الْمَلَاعِق وَالشُّوَك وَالسَّكَاكِين هُنَاكَ، فِي الدُّرْج الْأَوَّل.
lines.en: The spoons, the forks and the knives are over there, in the first drawer.

lines.ar: يَا سَامِي، الْمَلَاعِق هُنَا كَثِيرَة جِدًّا! كَمْ مِلْعَقَةً نُرِيدُ؟
lines.en: Sami, there are so many spoons here! How many spoons do we need?

lines.ar: سَبْعَ مَلَاعِق وَسَبْعَ شُوَك. لَا نُرِيدُ السَّكَاكِين الْيَوْم.
lines.en: Seven spoons and seven forks. We don't need the knives today.

lines.ar: وَالْخُبْز؟ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ أَرْغِفَة كَافِيَة لِلْجَمِيع؟
lines.en: And the bread? Do you have enough loaves for everyone?

lines.ar: طَبْعًا! عِنْدَنَا عَشَرَة أَرْغِفَة طَازَجَة مِنَ الْمَخْبَز.
lines.en: Of course! We have ten fresh loaves from the bakery.

lines.ar: مَا شَاءَ اللّٰه! الطَّاوِلَة جَمِيلَة، وَالْأَطْبَاق كَثِيرَة وَلَذِيذَة.
lines.en: How wonderful! The table looks beautiful, and there are so many tasty dishes.

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلُوا! عِنْدَنَا مُلُوخِيَّة وَأَرُزّ وَدَجَاج وَخُضَار.
lines.en: Please help yourselves! We have molokhia, rice, chicken and vegetables.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا خَالَة! كُلُّ الْأَطْبَاق لَذِيذَة جِدًّا.
lines.en: Thank you very much, Auntie! All the dishes are really delicious.

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، أُمِّي أَحْسَنُ طَبَّاخَة فِي الْقَاهِرَة!
lines.en: Daniel, my mother is the best cook in all of Cairo!

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا حَبِيبِي! كُلُوا، كُلُوا… الطَّعَام كَثِير!
lines.en: Thank you, my dear! Eat, eat… there is plenty of food!
segs: my dear, my darling (to a man)

reading.title: Laying the table
reading.ar: عَلَى الطَّاوِلَة سَبْعَة صُحُون وَسَبْعَة أَكْوَاب. الْمَلَاعِق وَالشُّوَك بِجَانِبِ الصُّحُون. فِي الْوَسَط عَشَرَة أَرْغِفَة وَأَطْبَاق كَثِيرَة.
reading.en: On the table there are seven plates and seven glasses. The spoons and forks are next to the plates. In the middle there are ten loaves and lots of dishes.

quiz.prompt: What is the plural of كِتَاب (book)?
How many people are at dinner?
Choose the correct sentence: 'The plates are big.'
Which word starts with the throat sound ʿayn?
Which word do you use for 'they' when you talk about plates?

completion: Brilliant! You can name the things on a table and use broken plurals. Tomorrow: two of everything, with the dual.
